title: ALMA observations of cold molecular gas filaments trailing rising radio bubbles in PKS 0745-191
question: What are the distribution, kinematics and origin of the cold molecular gas in the PKS 0745-191 BCG, and is it lifted by radio bubbles, cooled in situ, or inflowing?

data.sensitivity: rms 0.6 mJy (CO(1-0)) and 1 mJy (CO(3-2)) per 10 km/s channel

what.value: IRAM 30m CO(1-0) flux 1.8±0.4 Jy km/s and single-dish mass

evidence.quote: IRAM $30\rm\; m$ single dish signal of $1.8\pm0.4\hbox{$\rm\; Jy\rm\; km\rm\; s^{-1}\,$}$ ((cite: Salome03))

what.value: X-ray cooling rate 270±90 Msun/yr, hot gas pressure, g, metallicity

evidence.quote: the X-ray cooling rate of $270\pm90\hbox{$\hbox{$\rm\thinspace M_{\odot}$}\rm\; yr^{-1}\,$}$ determined from XMM-RGS spectroscopy ((cite: Sanders14))
estimated from the K-band effective radius of $9.5\rm\; arcsec$ given by the 2MASS extended source catalogue

recipe.method: ALMA pipeline calibration in CASA, self-calibration, CLEAN continuum-subtracted cubes with Briggs weighting
Single Gaussian fit to spectra from 6''x6'' (CO 1-0) and 4''x4'' (CO 3-2) regions, corrected for primary beam and instrumental broadening
Convolve CO(3-2) to CO(1-0) beam, fit integrated intensities in K km/s in matched regions, ratio
assumptions: optically thick, thermalized CO gives excitation temperature

recipe.method: Fit one or two Gaussians to beam-sized spectra at each pixel; require 3 sigma detection via Monte Carlo
assumptions: systemic velocity from optical emission lines (z=0.1028)

recipe.method: Position-velocity cuts along each CO(3-2) filament, summed across 0.2-0.3 arcsec width
M_mol from CO(1-0) integrated intensity with Galactic X_CO
assumptions: X_CO = 2e20 cm^-2 (K km/s)^-1; filament masses assume CO(1-0) and CO(3-2) distributed similarly

recipe.method: Hernquist-potential free-fall velocity vs radius, varying inclination
key_parameters: scale radius 10 kpc; total mass ~2e12 Msun (X-ray) or 1.8e13 (lensing)

evidence.quote: the total molecular gas mass is $(4.6\pm0.3)\times10^9\hbox{$\rm\thinspace M_{\odot}$}$
The SE filament is likely the most massive with $\sim1.9\times10^{9}\hbox{$\rm\thinspace M_{\odot}$}$.

not_stated_but_needed: Line-free channels used for continuum subtraction
Self-calibration solution intervals and number of iterations
Clean masks, thresholds, image size and cell size
Flux calibrator and flux scale uncertainty
Channel binning applied to each cube
Distance/luminosity distance value used in mass formula
Exact region definitions for filaments (beyond figures)
missing_for_reproduction: Region definitions for spectral extraction in filaments
score_reason: Public data and a fairly clear recipe with key numbers, but imaging and self-calibration details are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, simple Gaussian fits and mass formula, numeric results such as the 4.6e9 Msun mass and line ratios.
